answer: Ephemeral work-credential chaining. Each agent identity is issued a jade token embedded in a short-lived hash chain: to act, it must present a credential co-signed by the counterparty of its previous transaction, so signatures link into an unbroken ridge of verified exchanges. Cloning requires each fake identity to complete a genuine prior trade before it can act, forcing attackers to pay real settlement costs and counterparty risk per clone. An invalid link raises the chain's delta, flagging the identity for exclusion from matching until the gap is resolved.
